messages:
maggie: quick flag FYI — after the kernel-selection change yesterday we're seeing an unexpected drop in prefix cache hit-rate and a couple of GPU OOMs on staging. rolling back now but want to log details here.
ryan: thanks. can you paste the top-line metrics? hit-rate, mem delta, and which kernel was picked?
sasha: 👀 also throw the batching config. last time batching heuristics interacted weirdly with kv key normalization.
maggie: hit-rate (top-100k prefixes) went 86% -> 49%. GPU mem on p3-2x nodes jumped ~2.1GB per pod, fragmentation visible in nvidia-smi dmon. kernel tag that landed: compile-kernel-v3 (opt-prefetch + fused-attn fastpath).
ryan: ugh. that kernel enables a prefetch path that changes the prompt serialization order for KV keys, right? could be accidental key salt change.
maggie: exactly. discovered that the new fastpath uses a different hash input: we included a transient batch-id in the key material when continuous-batching=true. bug.
devon: that would explain lower hit-rate. more unique keys -> less reuse -> cache churn -> more allocations -> OOM. can you test toggling continuous-batching=false?
maggie: toggled on a staging pool (10 pods) — immediate hit-rate recovered to ~83% and mem stabilized. reverting kernel in prod now. logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:03:21Z] kernel=compile-kernel-v3 batch_mode=continuous true kv_key_hash=sha256(prefix||batch_id)
[2026-03-15T14:03:25Z] kv.hit_rate=0.49 kv.entries=1.9M gpu_mem=11.8GB
[2026-03-15T14:05:12Z] kernel=compile-kernel-v2 batch_mode=continuous=false kv_key_hash=sha256(prefix)
[2026-03-15T14:05:20Z] kv.hit_rate=0.83 kv.entries=1.1M gpu_mem=9.6GB
```
ryan: nice repro. plan: patch kernel to stop including batch_id in key material, add unit tests for keying, and add a perf test that asserts hit-rate doesn't drop >5% on the top-100k prefix workload.
anika: also let's add a defensive eviction TTL ramp while we patch. suggestion: increase prefix TTL from 300s -> 1800s for affected clusters and add soft-lru hysteresis. that reduces churn while we roll.
sasha: agree. propose hysteresis: when eviction pressure > 70% of configured mem, increase TTL for recently hot keys by factor 3 for 10 minutes. add metric kv.eviction_pressure to console.
devon: one more: fragmentation. the fastpath changed allocation sizes (more small slabs). we should run a slab compaction job after the rollback and add a periodic slab defrag in the runtime when fragmentation > 30%.
infra-bot: deploy started: rollback/compile-kernel-v2 -> staging(10) at 1865432200 by maggie.
maggie: post-rollback numbers look good so far. also instrumented a canary check that compares sha256(key) before storing vs after; it will alert if key canonicalization changes.
ryan: checklist for next PR: 1) remove batch_id from key construction (code link) 2) add unit + perf tests 3) temp TTL ramp + hysteresis in config 4) slab compaction job + fragmentation alert 5) update changelog and call out perf regression risk.
sasha: putting that into a short RFC so infra and runtime teams sign off. I'll include charts for hit-rate by prefix cohort (top1k/top10k/top100k) and memory delta.
anika: I'll coordinate with SRE on cluster TTL change and follow up on runbook updates (what to do if hit-rate drops suddenly).
devon: and we should add a small invariant to CI that prevents new kernels from touching KV keying without explicit opt-in.
maggie: thanks all. I'll post the PR and tag reviewers. leaving the canary up for a couple hours and will ping when ready to promote. :thumbsup:
